$comment: The source of sf-skeleton's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/skeleton (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

kind.summary: What shape the placeholder takes: a line of text, a circle, a square or a rounded block.

type.summary: type="icon" marks a placeholder that stands in for an icon; it combines with any kind. Not a legacy name for kind (see contracts/public-api-axes.json), so it has no removal date.

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16).

accessibility.name: none
accessibility.$comment: The placeholder geometry is aria-hidden: it has no role and no name. The region that waits for data says it is busy (aria-busy) and names itself; the skeleton draws only.

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-skeleton for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard §16 item 20). mode: same-detail (the shim sends the new and the old name), detail-adds (the new detail holds the old fields), attribute-and-property, host-attribute (no shim), manifest-only (the DOM name does not change), retired (no new name; kept and noted by the component until the date).

rows.summary: Legacy name for kind, still honoured. See contracts/public-api-axes.json.

x-summary: Decorative loading placeholder that reserves source-backed content geometry with semantic tokens and reduced-motion support.
x-renamed: settings.variant: the kind axis's old name, a dated setting alias of kind
x-decisions: version: 1.0.0 → 1.1.0: variant is a dated alias of kind; a minor while it holds (§4.10).
a11y-role: none. The generated placeholder geometry is aria-hidden; the region that waits says aria-busy and names itself.
a11y-name: none, for the same reason: nothing is read out (§4.8 allows "none").
number-type: count is an integer from 1 to 20, as the template clamps it.
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows.

skeleton: sf-skeleton is CSS bars drawn from settings only; it needs no skeleton.html of its own, its static markup is its first paint (§5.4). A component with late data writes its own skeleton.html; sf-skeleton is what a page draws by hand.
items: kept as a string of attribute sets (name=value, … | …); only aria-* and data-* attributes reach the bars.
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json plus the shapes and the animations; probe.json checks the count, the hidden geometry and the alias.
css-variables: five public variables read by the class sheet with the role token as fallback (src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json).

version 1.1.1: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-skeleton while content with predictable geometry is loading. Match the expected text, avatar, media or card shape closely and set aria-busy on the host content region until replacement is complete.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component
Do not use Skeleton as progress, empty, success or error feedback
Do not make placeholder geometry focusable or announce each shape
Do not use literal dimensions when a Framework token exists
Do not keep aria-busy true after real content is ready

accessibility.focus: Skeleton is not interactive and never enters the tab order. The host content region owns aria-busy and any spoken loading status.

setState.summary: Writes each key as its kebab-case attribute: false, null, undefined or an empty string removes it, true sets it empty, anything else is stringified.
